text:
Operators of pension sector under the auspices of Nigeria’s Pension Industry Leadership Council (PILC), has made good its promise to embark on massive investment in infrastructural development by signing an agreement with a UK-funded specialist development agency, FSD Africa, to support the development of a proposed $750 million infrastructure fund.
This was disclosed by the pension sector regulator, the National Pension Commission( PenCom) in a statement.
The fund according g the commission aims to bring together capital from Nigerian pension funds and development finance to invest in infrastructure projects in Nigeria and selected markets across the
PenCom, said the partnership reflected a shared UK-Nigeria ambition to deepen Nigeria’s capital markets, mobilise more domestic investment and channel long-term capital into the real economy.
In a statement released by the National Pension Commission, the initiative developed by Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs), with support from the National Pension Commission (PenCom) and FSD Africa, has attracted interest from 19 Nigerian pension funds, signalling strong appetite to put more long-term domestic capital to work in infrastructure.
UK Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, said UK was proud to partner with the Nigeria’s Pension Industry and the pensions regulator Pencom to progress this investment.
“Both our countries are prioritising tacking the challenge of attracting more domestic capital, including from pension funds, into the real economy. It is great to see Nigeria making concrete progress on its efforts and be a part of those opportunities to turn this ambition into investment, jobs, and economic growth,” Baxter said.
Also speaking, Chairman Nigeria Pension Industry Leadership Council and Director General National Pension Commission (PenCom), Ms Omolola Oloworaran,welcomed the proposed platformn as one whose timing and ambition could not be more ideal.
FSD Africa CEO Mark Napier, in his comment termed the planned new investment structure as one with great promise for Nigeria and Africa.
“We have observed for several years now the paradox of Africa having significant institutional capital while at the same time facing big infrastructure funding deficits. We are keen to work with PenCom and the pension industry in Nigeria to address this and unlock the capital they manage towards Nigeria’s priority infrastructure.” Mark said
